h1: The 4 Best GE Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four GE microwaves, from a 1150W countertop model to over-the-range units, compared on wattage, capacity and venting.
summary: The GE 1150 watt countertop is the best overall, with the highest wattage here and no installation. The 30 inch over-the-range model replaces an existing built-in, while the 1.9 cu. ft. unit has the biggest cavity and a 400 CFM convertible vent. The GE Profile low profile model suits tight clearance with its 1.2 cu. ft. cavity.
intro: Shopping a GE microwave by wattage alone is the quickest way to the wrong box. A countertop unit and an over-the-range unit can carry similar power ratings and still be wrong for the same kitchen, because one needs counter space and the other needs a vent path, a mounting plate and a free 30 inch opening above the stove. The decision is about installation first, cooking power second.

Our editors reviewed GE's current listings and ranked four that cover the real decision points: countertop versus over-the-range, cavity size, vent strength and clearance. Scores follow the published specifications. Where a listing is sparse, such as the countertop model's feature list, we note it, and we left out models that did not state a power figure.

products.name: GE Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A high-wattage countertop GE with no installation fuss.
products.description:
The countertop GE lists 1150 watts and a 1.6 cu. ft. cavity, which makes it the most powerful microwave in this ranking. Power determines how quickly a plate of leftovers reaches the middle, and a 150 watt gap over the 1000 watt built-ins shortens reheats noticeably. You plug it in and it works.

It ranks first because it combines the highest cooking power with zero installation, no vent run and no mounting bracket. The over-the-range units give back counter space but cost more and cook at 1000 watts.

Buy it if you rent, live in an apartment, or want strong, simple reheating. The caveats are counter space and a thin feature listing: it offers no hood vent and no cooktop light, so it does nothing for the area above your stove.
products.idealFor: Renters and apartment cooks who want strong, simple reheating.
products.skipIf: You want a hood vent and light above your stove.

products.name: GE 30" Over-the-Range Microwave
products.verdict: The standard replacement for a 30 inch built-in microwave.
products.description:
This 30 inch over-the-range GE is the standard replacement for a built-in microwave. A 1.6 cu. ft. cavity sits above a 300 CFM hood vent with LED cooktop lighting, and it frees the counter by doubling as the range hood. At 1000 watts it cooks a little slower than the countertop model.

It ranks second because cooking power drops and installation is required, and its 300 CFM vent trails the 400 CFM fans on the two models below. If the existing opening is 30 inches wide, though, the swap is straightforward.

Choose it when you have a matching 30 inch spot and a mounting bracket on the wall. Skip it if you rent. A 300 CFM fan handles light cooking, but a stove used daily for frying will want the stronger vent from the 1.9 cu. ft. unit.
products.idealFor: Homeowners replacing an existing 30 inch over-range microwave.
products.skipIf: You rent or have no wall-mounted bracket.

products.name: GE Over the Range Microwave Oven with 1.9 cu. ft. Capacity
products.verdict: The biggest cavity and stronger vent for busy stoves.
products.description:
The 1.9 cu. ft. GE has the largest cavity of the four, 400 CFM of airflow and convertible venting, which lets you route air outside or recirculate it through a filter. Ten power levels give finer control over defrosting and gentle reheats, and cooking power is 1000 watts.

It ranks third behind the 1.6 cu. ft. model for fit, not features: a bigger body is harder to place in a tight cabinet opening. For frequent cooks, the stronger vent and larger cavity win.

Buy it for a family kitchen with a busy range, where large casserole dishes and steam are daily realities. The caveat: it needs installation and a wall bracket, and its 1000 watts is lower than the countertop's 1150. Measure the opening before ordering, because the cavity grows into available space.
products.idealFor: Families cooking big dishes over a busy range.

products.name: GE Profile 30" Over-the-Range Low Profile Microwave
products.verdict: A shallower GE for tight spaces above the range.
products.description:
The GE Profile low profile is a 30 inch over-the-range model with a 1.2 cu. ft. cavity, 1000 watts, a 400 CFM vent and LED lighting. The shallower body leaves more headroom above the burners, which is the point in kitchens with low cabinets.

It ranks last because the cavity is the smallest here. It does keep the 400 CFM vent that the standard 1.6 cu. ft. model lacks, so you trade interior space for stronger ventilation and a slimmer look.

Buy it if clearance above the range is limited but you still want a strong fan. Skip it if you need to fit large dinner plates. A 1.2 cu. ft. cavity can struggle with a 12 inch plate, so check the interior diameter against the dishes you heat most often.
products.idealFor: Kitchens with limited clearance above the range.
products.skipIf: You need to fit large dinner plates.

whatMatters.detail: A countertop unit plugs in and sits on your counter, while an over-the-range unit mounts above the stove and doubles as a vent. The wrong choice costs counter space or an installation. Check your wall for a mounting bracket and a standard 30 inch opening before buying, and confirm the outlet location, since over-the-range units need one inside the cabinet.

Wattage is the power the microwave uses to heat food. Higher wattage cooks faster, and a 900 watt unit takes noticeably longer than an 1150 watt one for the same plate. Look for the cooking wattage in the product title or bullet list, not the marketing copy, because input power and cooking power differ. A bigger label number does not always mean faster cooking.

Capacity is the interior volume in cubic feet. Under 1.4 cu. ft. can struggle with a standard dinner plate, while 1.9 cu. ft. handles large dishes. Check the interior diameter and the turntable size if you plan to heat big plates or casseroles. Bigger cavities cost more installation space as well, and add weight to the bracket.

CFM measures how much air the hood fan moves. A busy stove benefits from 400 CFM, while 300 CFM is acceptable for light cooking. Look for the figure and for whether the unit vents outside or recirculates. Recirculating models rely on a filter that needs regular cleaning, while ducted ones clear steam faster.

Over-the-range models are typically 30 inches wide and need minimum clearance above the burners. A low profile unit helps when you are tight on headroom. Measure the opening and the height from the cooktop to the cabinet before ordering, and check the manufacturer's installation clearance rather than guessing. Skipping this step is why many installs fail.

faq.q: Can an over-the-range GE replace a countertop one?
faq.a: Only if you can mount it above the stove. An over-the-range GE needs a bracket, an electrical outlet and a venting plan, so it is not a drop-in swap for a countertop model. Plan for a helper to lift it.

faq.q: What is the common mistake when buying a GE microwave?
faq.a: Ignoring width and clearance. Always measure the opening, since 30 inches is the usual over-range standard, and check the headroom above the cooktop before choosing between the 1.6, 1.9 and 1.2 cu. ft. models. Photos make them look similar.

faq.q: Is the GE Profile worth it over the standard 30 inch model?
faq.a: It gives a stronger 400 CFM vent in a low profile body, but its 1.2 cu. ft. cavity is smaller than the standard model's 1.6 cu. ft. Choose it for clearance and ventilation, not capacity, and expect to heat smaller plates.

faq.q: How do I set up convertible venting?
faq.a: The 1.9 cu. ft. GE supports both outside venting and recirculation, so choose based on your ductwork. Venting outside clears steam better, while recirculation depends on a filter that needs cleaning.

faq.q: How do I maintain an over-the-range GE?
faq.a: Wash or replace the grease filter regularly, and wipe the cavity after spills. A clogged filter cuts airflow on the over-the-range models, so check it every few months, especially if you fry often.

faq.q: Can a countertop GE heat large dishes?
faq.a: The 1150 watt model has a 1.6 cu. ft. cavity, which handles standard plates. Very large dishes may need the 1.9 cu. ft. unit, though that is an over-the-range model, so it brings installation with it.

finalTake: Buy the countertop GE unless a built-in is already in your kitchen. Choose the 1.9 cu. ft. over-the-range unit for big dishes and a busy stove, the 30 inch 1.6 cu. ft. model for a like-for-like replacement, and the Profile when clearance is tight.
